name: Legacy Transform -- one workflow that takes an existing product, walks every resource composing it, renders its canonical LGIC form beside the current one, marks it, and hands back a structured contract, a flow diagram, the typed tensions and a remediation plan
description: D14's fourth project, the LENS. Commissioned by Andrew-direct 2026-09-16 ~05:1xZ at the 4.0.0_SA_CRO terminal ('the premise of which is LGIC_LGCTFM. The idea is its legacy transform ... something like /atom-decomp and /canonical-flow combined') and named by him. It is the instrument every R19 migration consumes: subject in; a walk across both trigger APIs, all compute, identity, storage, messaging, the two declared planes, the Terraform tree and the served routes; a CURRENT half measured per row and a DESIRED half computed by lib/opal_naming.py address()/name()/grade(), never typed; forks found by the desired twin; tensions typed by axis x rule with the tension map's four factors measured; two /draw diagrams generated from the contract; the plan as ATOM_DECOMP atomic packages in R19's six-step order; the MARK written into the three registries the naming gate and builders already read. It moves nothing: every act its output names is a separate R19 project under its own sign-off.

A round cut against outcomes that bar outside the engine is the 'hardening round that quietly implies progress it cannot make' this project's own round-2 analysis warned about. If an IN-ENGINE outcome a round could move appears, it is a new round on its own merit, never a continuation. --- WHY THIS ROW WAS STALE, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED, AND THE BAR IT CORRECTS: this carrier's most recent recorded close was ROUND 2 while analyses existed for rounds 3 through 9 and round 10 sat at L8 -- SEVEN CLOSED ROUNDS.
